title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 165
paragraphs: When these Phocaeans reached Corsica, they lived for five years alongside the earlier settlers and founded temples. But they plundered all their neighbors, so the Etruscans and Carthaginians joined forces against them. Each brought sixty ships, making a total of one hundred and twenty against the Phocaeans' sixty. They fought a sea battle off the Sardinian coast. The Phocaeans won, but it was a hollow victory: they lost forty ships, and the remaining twenty had their rams bent and were useless. They sailed back to Alalia, picked up their women, children, and whatever possessions they could carry, abandoned Corsica, and sailed to the Italian mainland, where they founded the city of Velia.
